guidance.condition: Confirmed later: the 40-45% does not count on RIP cores from the new plant (p.16). The CMD separately put FY27 invoicing at ₹360-400 Cr (p.20), which is 53-70% over FY26's ₹235 Cr; the two figures do not reconcile.

insights.summary: FY26 was a record: revenue rose 57% to ₹235 Cr, EBITDA 75% to ₹60 Cr (25.7% margin) and PAT 75% to ₹37 Cr, with an order book above ₹400 Cr. The CMD guides FY27 revenue growth of 40-45% and an EBITDA margin around 24-25% as new-plant costs come in, with margins rising from FY28; later in the call he put FY27 invoicing at ₹360-400 Cr, which implies faster growth. The Jarod RIP plant (now designed up to 550 kV) is due for trial production by September and commercial production from October. Order booking of ₹500 Cr+ is targeted for FY27, and an equity raise of ₹100-110 Cr is planned.

what_changed.text: Growth outlook lifted to 40-42% a year for 4-5 years (from 35%+ CAGR)
FY27: 40-45% revenue growth and ~24-25% EBITDA margin; ₹360-400 Cr invoicing target
Greenfield commercial production in H2 FY27, now targeted for October
Equity raise of ₹100-110 Cr (approval for ₹150 Cr)
Sukrut Electric acquisition closed; ₹150-160 Cr revenue aim in 4-5 years

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: We are confident for that growth.

analyst_questions.answer: 40-45% without counting on in-house RIP cores; ₹360-400 Cr invoicing target.
~24-25% in FY27 with new-plant costs, rising from FY28 on localisation and exports.
The CMD prefers to stay debt-free and wants good investors on the cap table.
Funds lost in a cyber fraud were expensed; a police complaint is under investigation.

red_flags.text: Two FY27 revenue figures that don't reconcile: 40-45% growth (₹329-341 Cr) vs ₹360-400 Cr invoicing.
Equity raise of ₹100-110 Cr dilutes holders despite low debt.
A cyber fraud loss was expensed; amount not given on the call.
Supply chain and staff attrition named as the main limits to growth.
